correctness.rationale: The tree with L_k=2^ka_k exists because b_k=2a_(k+1)/a_k is 1,2 or 4, and B* maps each parent onto a normalized sum of its disjoint children: BB*=I. Its isometric adjoint is pure (ranges supported beyond depth n), and infinite splitting makes ker B infinite dimensional; Wold identifies the backward coisometry class. Directly KK* e_v=2^(-2k-2)e_v, so 2^(-k-1) has multiplicity 2^ka_k. Completed-rank sums are 1/2 sum_(j≤k)a_j and log M_k=k log2+O(1), giving both lim extrema. Superexponential alternating blocks achieve means 1 and 2 while nonbinary branching has zero level density. The S_p condition p>1 and nonconvergent Connes-Dixmier measurability conclusion follow analytically, not from sample levels.
